comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: 2026-10-16: Muster's encoding is right (d6435d94 pins it): Ctrl+Return reaches the daemon as Ghostty's app builds it, and a program in Claude Code's mode (CSI < u, CSI > 5 u, CSI > 4;2 m) receives ESC[13;5u, as from Ghostty. The one link no test covers is AppKit in a real key window: Ghostty's view catches Ctrl+Return in performKeyEquivalent ('prevent the default context menu equivalent'), and Muster's has no such override. By hand: in a Muster pane and in Ghostty, printf '\e[>5u\e[>4;2m'; cat -v, then Ctrl+Return - both should print ^[[13;5u. If Muster prints nothing, port Ghostty's performKeyEquivalent case. Meanwhile Claude Code's ctrl+x ctrl+s sends a queued line now.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body: 2026-10-21: fixed on main in 73a1352b by porting Ghostty's performKeyEquivalent case: the pane's view claims ctrl+return as a keystroke while it has the keyboard, after asking the main menu first so a [keymap] binding on ctrl+return still wins. 3 tests. Not yet tried in the real app. By hand on a build of main: printf '\\e[>5u\\e[>4;2m'; cat -v, then ctrl+return prints ^[[13;5u and no context menu opens; and in Claude Code, a line typed while it works is sent at once by ctrl+return. Move to done once seen.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
amterp, Chat Notes 2026-10-15: "Claude asks for Ctrl enter but muster maybe hijacks".

Claude Code queues a line typed while it works and offers `ctrl+enter to send now` (`docs/observations/claude-code-2.1.288.md`, section 1). In Muster 0.16.0 that seems not to work. Neither the default keymap nor `~/.muster/config.toml` binds ctrl+return, so the key is likelier mis-encoded than taken.

Suspect: c21d7b3e, in 0.16.0 a day before the note, sends any key whose character is a control character with no text, as Ghostty's macOS app does. Its message says Ctrl+Return "may also change in legacy mode... that was not checked". Claude Code turns on the kitty keyboard protocol, so compare what a program in that mode receives in Muster and in Ghostty: `printf "\e[>1u"; cat -v`, then Ctrl+Return.

Not yet reproduced. a_2hIfseida's by-hand check of Shift+Tab on 0.16.0 can be done in the same session.
title: Ctrl+Return does not reach Claude Code in a pane
